text.text_excerpt: I love the Steamboat Natchez!! It is a great way to kick back relaxing for a few hours, see the sights along the Mississippi River from a gorgeous old paddle boat. It's an experience that is Totally New Orleans! I've been on the boat only 3 times in my life, but if you spend any time in the French Quarter, the sight of the Natchez and the sounds of the calliope singing loud and proud are always a piece of the background near Decatur St. My first ride was in 3rd grade. A field-trip that I still remember 40 years later. When we got married a few years back we decided to take a cruise on the river as our day-after the wedding group activity. Wanna take a ride down the Mississippi River in a charming steamboat? Yes please! My husband and I boarded the Steamboat Natchez while visiting New Orleans. It was my first visit to the city so I was on board for a tour. We opted for the Sunday Brunch cruise sans the actual brunch. We sat outside on the deck and enjoyed a cocktail while listening to the narrator. We chose to skip the brunch because we preferred to just grab lunch somewhere else afterwards. You're in NOLA! There's tons of great eateries everywhere. We really enjoyed ourselves! It was a great way to chill and relax a bit while doing something "touristy". Second time on the Natchez. First time we just went along for the ride. This time did the Sunday jazz brunch cruise. So glad we did. Get there early (at least 30 mins) to get in line so that you get a good seat inside. We lucked out and got one by the window. Cruise was $40 but well worth it since its buffet and you can eat for the whole two hour ride up and down the Mississippi River. Food was really good, faves were creamed spinach with artichokes, cheese grits and the biscuits. They had bread pudding and a sweet red cake, not sure what flavor it was but it was good.
